references.text: Gideon also asked the men of Peniel for bread, just as he had done in Succoth, and received a similar rejection
Gideon fulfilled his threat and tore down the tower at Peniel, just as he had promised in verse 9
Peniel is the place where Jacob wrestled with God and named the place Penuel, which means 'face of God'
Peniel is mentioned as a city that Jeroboam rebuilt, showing the importance of the location
Gideon's threat against Succoth parallels his threat against Peniel - both refused to help and both were punished
